core.title: Declare the train family that matches its terminal contract
core.given: A train definition (new, edited or existing) declares a terminal contract
core.when: the planner authors, edits, reviews or validates that train definition
core.then: Ensure the train declares family:delivery if and only if the terminal requires an Acceptance Authority commit AND the terminal primary is platform:acceptance:commit-receipt, and family:behavior otherwise.
prefer: Decide the terminal contract first, then derive the family from it; the family is controlled redundancy that mirrors the terminal contract.
When editing a terminal contract, update the family in the same change so the two stay consistent.
avoid: Omitting the family field — a missing family is invalid, not a default.
Declaring family:delivery when only one of the two conditions holds (Acceptance Authority commit required, primary = platform:acceptance:commit-receipt).
Treating the family as a second source of truth that overrides or diverges from the terminal contract.
core.why: The family is fixed by the terminal contract; keeping it as checked, controlled redundancy (not an independent source of truth) prevents trains being routed or validated under the wrong family.
evidence: Each train definition has a family field present.
family is delivery exactly when terminal requires an Acceptance Authority commit and terminal primary == platform:acceptance:commit-receipt; behavior in every other case.
verification: Biconditional check over every train definition (not only changed ones): recompute the family implied by the declared terminal contract and report a finding whenever the declared family differs from it.
A missing family field is itself a finding (invalid), regardless of the terminal contract.
The check is realized as a validator; its concrete binding — and any pending-binding status — is a per-realization fact, not part of the core.
Covers only train definitions; other plan artifacts that carry no family/terminal fields are out of scope.

fires: A train's terminal requires an Acceptance Authority commit and its terminal primary is platform:acceptance:commit-receipt, but family is declared as behavior.
A train is declared family:delivery while its terminal does not require an Acceptance Authority commit, or its terminal primary is something other than platform:acceptance:commit-receipt.
A train definition has no family field at all.
An existing, untouched train definition encountered during planning or validation already has a family that disagrees with its terminal contract, or lacks a family field.
doesNotFire: A train with an Acceptance Authority commit terminal whose primary is platform:acceptance:commit-receipt, declared family:delivery.
A train whose terminal does not satisfy both delivery conditions, declared family:behavior.
Planning artifacts that are not train definitions (wagons, WMBTs, acceptances, docs) with no family/terminal fields.

neutralityNotes: The obligation is almost entirely ATDD-method vocabulary rather than stack mechanics, so the core keeps it verbatim: 'train definition' (a plan artifact), 'terminal contract', the family values delivery/behavior, 'Acceptance Authority commit' and the reserved terminal primary 'platform:acceptance:commit-receipt' are shared method constants, not stack structure, so they stay in the core instead of becoming profile keys (no vocabulary key fits them, and none is needed). What is Bun-only: the concrete train-definition schema field paths in the checker pseudocode (verifier_detail[0]), the validator test ref and pending-binding ticket D1/#1085 (evidence[2], verifier_detail[3]), and the term id family_consistency (verifier_detail[2]). The Bun activation fact 'layer: planning' is rendered as the neutral fact type 'phase'. Per-rule severity (3) and disposition (strict) live in core.verification per the not-profile-keys rule. The only structural need is resolving 'train definition' to concrete files, supplied by roles.plan_artifact.kinds.
